newsitem.title: POLAND: Espebepe creditor eyes debt compromise.
newsitem.headline: Espebepe creditor eyes debt compromise.

text.p: Polish Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA, the biggest creditor of the ailing Espebepe construction firm, spelled out a compromise debt reduction deal on Monday before Espebepe creditors meet for the last time on May 16.
Espebepe wants its largest creditors to write off 95 percent of its 75-million-zloty debt and then to raise the firm's capital by taking over a new share issue at five zlotys per share.
Pomorski, however, wants to write off 40 percent of the debt and turn the rest into a convertible bond issue, saying that injecting more money into Espebepe through a capital raise was unacceptable.
Espebepe's management has rejected Pomorski's offer as too expensive and time-consuming.
"We uphold our offer to write off 40 percent of the debt and strengthen the deal by changing the remaining debt into a convertible bond issue," Pomorski said in a Monday statement.

"A rise in Espebepe's share capital could be interesting under the condition that it would be combined with our offer and that the new share issue would be addressed to all potential buyers (not only creditors)," the statement said.
The next creditors meeting is scheduled for May 16, after two former ones on March 14 and April 14 failed to decide the fate of the firm.
Espebepe earlier said the May meeting would be the last one at which a decision on a debt-deal or bankruptcy must be taken.
"Talks started recently with Espebepe management allow the hope that a compromise (on the debt-reduction method) can be reached before the final vote," Pomorski's statement said.
Espebepe President Andrzej Hass told Reuters the company was open to all proposals which could save it from bankruptcy.
"We are waiting for proposals. We are open to all offers which could lead to saving the firm," Hass said on Monday.
